chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what is rejected from the witnesses. He said: The suspicious one, the accused one, and the adversary. I said: The immoral one and the treacherous one? He said: All of this is included in the suspicious one.

key_terms.الظَّنِينُ: The suspicious one (one whose testimony is suspect due to potential bias or defect)
key_terms.الْخَائِنُ: The treacherous one (one known for dishonesty or breach of trust)
key_terms.الْخَصْمُ: The adversary (one who has a direct opposing interest in the case)
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُ: The immoral one (one who commits sins openly)
key_terms.الْمُتَّهَمُ: The accused one (often referring to one of illegitimate birth or known defect)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for rejecting a witness in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential grounds for witness disqualification (shurut al-shuhud), emphasizing that credibility is compromised by suspicion of bias or deceit. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that specific moral failings like being 'fasiq' (immoral) or 'khanin' (treacherous) are not distinct categories but are encompassed within the broader legal concept of 'al-zannin' (one who is suspected). This hierarchical classification reflects the Shia scholarly approach to balancing textual evidence with practical judicial assessment of a witness's reliability.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about what from the witnesses are rejected. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The suspicious, and the accused (of being a bastard), and the adversary’ (opponents). I said, ‘(What about) the immoral and the treacherous?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘All this is included in the suspicious’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Shu’ayb from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the witnesses whose testimonies are rejected. He (the Imam) said, ‘He (the Imam) said, ‘Of such people are a pessimist, an accused and an antagonist.’ I then asked, ‘What about a sinful and a treacherous one?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Such ones are included in “pessimist”.”’
